The findings from these healthcare Q&A matches suggest that economic inequalities in breast and cervical cancer screening are low in lower-middle-income (LMIC) countries with high screening coverage. These studies indicate that even in countries with high income inequality, there is significant equity in cancer screening coverage.

In other words, the inverse equity hypothesis suggests that higher levels of coverage should be associated with greater equity in access to cancer screening services, particularly in LMICs. However, the matches also highlight that this relationship may not hold in every case, and further research is needed to better understand the complexities involved.
